root_cause: The header component incorrectly sets aria-hidden=true on the navigation menu when the page loads at desktop widths, causing the navigation links to be excluded from the accessibility tree.
repair_strategy: Modify the syncState method to only apply aria-hidden when the menu button is visible (i.e., in mobile/viewport where the navigation is hidden via CSS), preserving the default accessible state on desktop.
expected_accessibility_effect: Navigation links will be exposed as links in the accessibility tree, enabling screen reader and keyboard users to discover and activate them.
functional_risks: If the visibility check fails, the navigation could remain hidden from assistive technology on mobile when opened, or remain visible on desktop when it should be hidden. The check uses offsetWidth/offsetHeight which reliably reflects the button's CSS display state.
verification_requirements: After the fix, the ax assertion for the 'Apply' link must pass (role link, name 'Apply').
When the menu button is clicked in a narrow viewport, the navigation's aria-hidden attribute should toggle between true (closed) and false (open).
Ensure no regression in the visual presentation of the header across breakpoints.
